Liliʻuokalani.fact: Her bridemaids were her former classmates Elizabeth Kekaʻaniau and Martha Swinton.

Liliʻuokalani.question: The couple moved into the _____' residence, Washington Place in Honolulu
Liliʻuokalani.fact: The couple moved into the Dominises' residence, Washington Place in Honolulu.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The couple moved into the Dominises' residence, Washington Place in Honolulu. Through his wife and connections with the king, Dominis would later become Governor of Oʻahu and Maui.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: In _____, she and Pauahi helped Princess Victoria establish the Kaʻahumanu Society, a female-led organization aimed at the relief of the elderly and the ill
Liliʻuokalani.fact: In 1864, she and Pauahi helped Princess Victoria establish the Kaʻahumanu Society, a female-led organization aimed at the relief of the elderly and the ill.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: At the request of Kamehameha V, she composed "He Mele Lāhui Hawaiʻi" in _____ as the new Hawaiian national anthem
Liliʻuokalani.fact: At the request of Kamehameha V, she composed "He Mele Lāhui Hawaiʻi" in 1866 as the new Hawaiian national anthem.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: This was in use until replaced by her brother's composition "_____ʻi Ponoʻī"
Liliʻuokalani.fact: At the request of Kamehameha V, she composed "He Mele Lāhui Hawaiʻi" in 1866 as the new Hawaiian national anthem. This was in use until replaced by her brother's composition "Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī".

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: During the _____ visit of Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh and the Galatea, she entertained the British prince with a traditional Hawaiian luau at her Waikiki residence of Hamohamo
Liliʻuokalani.fact: During the 1869 visit of Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh and the Galatea, she entertained the British prince with a traditional Hawaiian luau at her Waikiki residence of Hamohamo.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: Following a non-binding referendum and subsequent unanimous vote in the legislature, _____ became the first elected king of Hawaii
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Following a non-binding referendum and subsequent unanimous vote in the legislature, Lunalilo became the first elected king of Hawaii. Lunalilo died without an heir in 1874.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: Lunalilo died without an heir in _____
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Lunalilo died without an heir in 1874.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: US and _____ troops were landed, and some of Emma's supporters were arrested
Liliʻuokalani.fact: US and British troops were landed, and some of Emma's supporters were arrested.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: The results of the election strained the relationship between _____ and the Kalākaua family
Liliʻuokalani.fact: In the election that followed, Liliʻuokalani's brother, David Kalākaua, ran against Emma, the dowager queen of Kamehameha IV. US and British troops were landed, and some of Emma's supporters were arrested.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: Leleiohoku died without an heir in _____
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Leleiohoku died without an heir in 1877.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: This would put the _____ back in succession to the throne again, which Kalākaua did not wish
Liliʻuokalani.fact: This would put the Kamehamehas back in succession to the throne again, which Kalākaua did not wish.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: On top of that, Kalākaua's court genealogists had already cast doubt on Ruth's direct lineage, and in doing so placed doubt on _____'s
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Leleiohoku's hānai (adoptive) mother, Ruth Keʻelikōlani, wanted to be named heir, but the king's cabinet ministers objected as that would place Bernice Pauahi Bishop, Ruth's first cousin, next in line. Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: In _____, Liliʻuokalani and Dominis sailed to California for her health
Liliʻuokalani.fact: In 1878, Liliʻuokalani and Dominis sailed to California for her health.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: They stayed in _____ and Sacramento where she visited the Crocker Art Museum
Liliʻuokalani.fact: They stayed in San Francisco and Sacramento where she visited the Crocker Art Museum.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: One of her first responsibilities was handling the smallpox epidemic of _____, likely brought to the islands by Chinese contracted laborers
Liliʻuokalani.fact: One of her first responsibilities was handling the smallpox epidemic of 1881, likely brought to the islands by Chinese contracted laborers.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: The measures kept the disease contained in _____ and Oʻahu with only a few cases on Kauaʻi
Liliʻuokalani.fact: The measures kept the disease contained in Honolulu and Oʻahu with only a few cases on Kauaʻi.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The disease mainly affected Native Hawaiians with the total number of cases at 789 with 289 fatalities, or a little over thirty-six percent.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: She was too overcome to speak and _____, one of her brother's ministers, had to address the people on her behalf
Liliʻuokalani.fact: She was too overcome to speak and John Makini Kapena, one of her brother's ministers, had to address the people on her behalf.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days

Liliʻuokalani.fact: She also convinced the governmental board of health to set aside land for a leprosy hospital at Kakaʻako.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: She made a second visit to the settlement with Queen Kapiʻolani in _____
Liliʻuokalani.fact: She made a second visit to the settlement with Queen Kapiʻolani in 1884.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: In _____, she founded a bank for women in Honolulu named Liliuokalani's Savings Bank and helped Isabella Chamberlain Lyman establish Kumukanawai o ka Liliuokalani Hui Hookuonoono, a money lending grou
Liliʻuokalani.fact: In 1886, she set up a bank for women in Honolulu named Liliuokalani's Savings Bank and helped Isabella Chamberlain Lyman establish Kumukanawai o ka Liliuokalani Hui Hookuonoono, a money lending group for women in Hilo.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: While in the _____ capital, they were received by President Grover Cleveland and his wife Frances Cleveland
Liliʻuokalani.fact: While in the American capital, they were received by President Grover Cleveland and his wife Frances Cleveland.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Queen Victoria greeted both Hawaiian royals with affection, and recalled Kalākaua's visit in 1881.

Liliʻuokalani.question: They canceled their tour of _____ and returned to Hawaii
Liliʻuokalani.fact: They canceled their tour of Europe and returned to Hawaii.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: and William R. Castle, members of the legislature's Reform (Missionary) Party, proposing her ascension to the throne if her brother Kalākaua were removed from power.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days

Liliʻuokalani.fact: In 1889, a part Native Hawaiian officer Robert W Wilcox, who resided in Liliʻuokalani's Palama residence, instigated an unsuccessful rebellion to overthrow the Bayonet Constitution.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The McKinley Tariff Act had crippled the Hawaiian sugar industry by removing the duties on sugar imports from other countries into the US, eliminating the previous Hawaiian duty-free advantage under the Reciprocity Treaty of 1875.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Traveling throughout Southern California and Northern Mexico, the monarch suffered a stroke in Santa Barbara and was rushed back to San Francisco.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Kalākaua fell into a coma in his suite on January 18, and died two days later on January 20. The official cause of death was "Bright's disease with Uremic Blood Poisoning." Liliʻuokalani.question: Supported by two-thirds of the registered voters, she moved to abrogate the existing _____ constitution, but her cabinet withheld their support, knowing what her opponents' likely response would be
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Supported by two-thirds of the registered voters, she moved to abrogate the existing 1887 constitution, but her cabinet withheld their support, knowing what her opponents' likely response would be.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: In response, royalists and loyalists formed the Committee of Law and Order and met at the palace square on January 16, 1893.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Nāwahī, White, Robert W. Wilcox, and other pro-monarchist leaders gave speeches in support for the queen and the government.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Wilson and captain of the Royal Household Guard Samuel Nowlein had rallied a force of 496 men who were kept at hand to protect the queen.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Marines from the USS Boston and two companies of US sailors landed and took up positions at the US Legation, the Consulate, and Arion Hall.

Liliʻuokalani.question: The sailors and _____ did not enter the palace grounds or take over any buildings, and never fired a shot, but their presence served effectively in intimidating royalist defenders
Liliʻuokalani.fact: Marines from the USS Boston and two companies of US sailors landed and took up positions at the US Legation, the Consulate, and Arion Hall. The sailors and Marines did not enter the palace grounds or take over any buildings, and never fired a shot, but their presence served effectively in intimidating royalist defenders.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The queen was deposed on January 17, and the provisional government set up under pro-annexation leader Sanford B. Liliʻuokalani.question: She temporarily relinquished her throne to the _____, rather than the Dole-led government, in hopes that the United States would restore Hawaii's sovereignty to the rightful holder
Liliʻuokalani.fact: She temporarily relinquished her throne to the United States, rather than the Dole-led government, in hopes that the United States would restore Hawaii's sovereignty to the rightful holder. A delegation departed for Washington, D.C., on January 19, to ask for immediate annexation by the United States.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The government under Dole began using ʻIolani Palace as its executive building.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: A delegation departed for _____, D.C., on January 19, to ask for immediate annexation by the United States
Liliʻuokalani.fact: A delegation departed for Washington, D.C., on January 19, to ask for immediate annexation by the United States.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The queen protested the proposed annexation in a January 19 letter to President Benjamin Harrison.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: She sent Prince David Kawānanakoa and Paul Neumann to represent her.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Her first response was that Hawaiian law called for property confiscation and the death penalty for treason, and that only her cabinet ministers could put aside the law in favor of amnesty.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The queen changed her position on the issue of amnesty, and on December 18, Willis demanded the provisional government reinstate her to the throne, but was refused.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: Congress responded with a US Senate investigation that resulted in the Morgan Report on February 26, 1894.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: It found Stevens and all parties except the queen "not guilty", absolving them of responsibility for the overthrow.

Liliʻuokalani.question: The provisional government formed the _____ of Hawaii on July 4 with Dole as its president, maintaining oligarchical control and a limited system of suffrage

Liliʻuokalani.fact: The sentence was commuted on September 4, to imprisonment in the palace, attended by her lady-in-waiting Eveline Townsend Wilson (aka Kitty), wife of Marshal Wilson.

Liliʻuokalani.fact: While in confinement she composed songs such as "The Queen's Prayer" (Ke Aloha o Ka Haku – "The Grace of the Lord").

Liliʻuokalani.fact: On October 13, 1896, the Republic of Hawaii gave her a full pardon and restored her civil rights. From December 1896 through January 1897, she stayed in Brookline, Massachusetts, with her husband's cousins William Lee and Sara White Lee, of the Lee & Shepard publishing house.

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: From December _____ through January 1897, she stayed in Brookline, Massachusetts, with her husband's cousins William Lee and Sara White Lee, of the Lee & Shepard publishing house

Liliʻuokalani.subject: Important Days
Liliʻuokalani.question: During this period her long-time friend _____
